D021-D016_h001.question:
I guess this has been going on maybe 6–8 months now. I started trying to “clean up” my eating because a bunch of guys at the plant were talking about heart issues and diabetes, and it kind of got into my head. Since then I’ve gotten really strict. I pretty much count everything I eat. I keep my daily intake as low as I can, sometimes to the point where my wife gets on my case about it. I’ve dropped a lot of weight, and she says I’m too thin, but I still feel like I should be careful and not put any back on.

What really stresses me is certain foods. Anything that feels heavy or greasy, or stuff like pizza, dessert, that kind of thing—I get this immediate worry that if I eat it, it’ll just sit there and turn into fat right away. I’ll replay it in my head, thinking about the calories and whether I “messed up,” and sometimes I’ll skip meals later or stick to very plain foods to “balance it out.” It’s not like I’m trying to look a certain way, exactly, but I feel uneasy if I don’t follow these rules I’ve set for myself.
D021-D016_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h001.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h002.question:
Honestly, this has been going on maybe six, seven months now. At first I just started skipping meals here and there, like telling myself I’d grab something later between fares, but now it’s kind of a pattern. I usually don’t eat breakfast at all, and if I do eat, it’s something small, and I’ll often find a reason to avoid lunch or dinner too, even if I feel a bit hungry.

My weight keeps dropping. My ex-wife saw me last month when I picked up our daughter and said I looked “drawn.” I keep checking myself on the scale at home, sometimes a few times a day. Even a small bump up freaks me out and I start replaying everything I ate, wondering what I did “wrong.”

Food in general has started to feel…complicated. I find myself going over and over what I’m allowed to eat, reading labels, planning, then re-planning. If I eat something I hadn’t planned, I feel so uncomfortable that I might skip the next meal to make up for it. It’s like my head gets stuck on it, and it’s hard to focus on driving or talking to passengers until I “fix” it somehow.
D021-D016_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h002.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h003.question:
It’s been maybe eight, nine months now that things with food have gotten…odd for me. I run a small company, so I’m used to structure, but this has gotten very rigid. I’ve cut out almost all bread, pasta, rice, anything fried, most oils. At first it was “just to be healthier,” but it’s become more and more strict, and if my wife serves something like potatoes or dessert, I get very tense and usually won’t touch it.

I’ve been gradually dropping weight over this period, not in a dramatic crash, but my belt keeps going down a notch every few weeks. I’m not skipping meals completely, but I eat very small portions and stick to the same “safe” foods over and over. If I even think about eating something I’ve labeled as “bad,” like pizza at a client dinner, I start running numbers in my head, imagining what it might do to me, and I feel almost panicky.

I also find myself checking labels repeatedly, planning meals in detail, and replaying what I ate that day, like I have to make sure it was “right,” even when I’m not sure what exactly I’m afraid of.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h003.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h004.question:

It started with skipping breakfast to “save time,” but now it’s most lunches too, especially on teaching days. Dinner with my wife is the only meal I reliably sit down for, and even then I keep the portions pretty small.

I weigh myself multiple times a day—before work, after I get home, sometimes again before bed. If the number goes up even half a kilo, I get this rush of panic and start replaying everything I ate, trying to figure out what I did “wrong.”

A lot of my thoughts now revolve around food and eating schedules—what I can or can’t have, how to “offset” a meal. It feels less like a choice and more like something I have to keep track of perfectly, or I get extremely uneasy.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

I find myself going over labels again and again, re-checking what I’ve eaten that day, planning meals in my head on long drives. It’s like I can’t relax unless I’ve gone through the numbers a few times.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D016_h006.question:

I tell myself those foods just slow me down, make me “foggy,” and I can’t afford that when I’m staring at charts all day.

If I eat something outside my rules, I get really uncomfortable until I “fix” it by skipping the next meal or doing some rigid routine. It’s getting harder to focus on trades because so much mental space is stuck on food and what I did or didn’t eat.

    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D021-D016_h007.question:

D021-D016_h009.question:
